prerequisites: Ability to work fluently with first and second-degree equations
Knowledge of the concept of differential and differential calculus
Knowledge of the notion of integral

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, and electromagnetism in a vacuum.
Ability to solve simple problems concerning mechanics, thermodynamics, and electromagnetism in a vacuum.

syllabus_topics: Introduction - Physical quantities - Dimensional equations - Systems of units - Scalar and vector quantities - Free vectors - Components of a vector - Sum of vectors - Product of a vector by a scalar - Scalar and vector product - Mixed product - Applied vectors - Polar moment - Axial moment - Vector operators - Flux - Line integral - Circulation - Divergence theorem - Stokes' (or curl) theorem

Kinematics of the material point - Reference systems - Geometric and temporal aspects of motion: trajectory and time equation - Displacements - Degrees of freedom - Examples of motion - Circular motion - Uniform circular motion - Harmonic motion - Average scalar velocity and instantaneous scalar velocity - Vector velocity - Average and instantaneous scalar acceleration, vector acceleration - Plane motions - Central motions - Theorem of relative motions - Coriolis theorem

Dynamics of the material point - Forces - Newton's laws - Inertial frames - Inertial mass - Fundamental forces and interactions - Momentum - Impulse of a force - Weight - Elastic forces - Constraint reactions - Friction - Passive resistances - Real and apparent forces: centrifugal force and Coriolis force - Simple pendulum

Work and energy for the material point - Definition of work - Power - Kinetic energy - Work-energy theorem - Conservative force fields - Potential energy - Conservation of mechanical energy - Energy in the harmonic oscillator - Variation of energy in the presence of non-conservative forces

Mechanics of systems of material points - Center of mass and motion of the center of mass - Momentum of a system - 1st cardinal equation - Third principle of dynamics - Total momentum - Internal and external forces - Principle of conservation of momentum - Motion of variable mass systems - Angular momentum - Angular momentum theorem for a system of points - Principle of conservation of angular momentum - 2nd cardinal equation - Work-energy theorem for a system of points - Total kinetic energy - Motion of the center of mass and motion around the center of mass - Potential energy in systems - Conservation of mechanical energy - Collision processes - Normal central collision - Collision in space

Mechanics of rigid bodies - Kinematics of rigid bodies - Rigid motions, translational motion, rotational motion - Distribution of velocities and accelerations in a rigid motion - Dynamics of rigid bodies - Equivalent force systems - Body rotating around a fixed axis - Moment of inertia - Axial moment of inertia - Examples of rotational motion around a fixed axis - Poinsot's theorem - Ellipsoid of inertia - Statics of rigid bodies - Cardinal equations of statics

Gravitation - Law of universal gravitation - Determination of the universal gravitation constant - Inertial mass and gravitational mass - Gravitational acceleration - Weight - Motion of planets and satellites - Kepler's laws - Gravitational field - Gauss' theorem - Gravitational potential energy - Mechanical energy in the solar system

Fluid Mechanics - Pressure at a point in a fluid - Equations of fluid statics - Statics of heavy fluids - Pascal's principle - Pressure measurement - Archimedes' principle - Fluid dynamics - Streamlines and flow lines - Work-energy theorem for ideal fluids - Bernoulli's equation - Continuity equation
Oscillations - Harmonic oscillator - Damped harmonic oscillator - Forced harmonic oscillator: resonance

First Principle of Thermodynamics - Systems and thermodynamic states - Thermodynamic equilibrium - Principle of thermal equilibrium - Definition of temperature - Thermometers - Adiabatic systems. Joule's experiments, Heat - First principle of thermodynamics. Internal energy - Thermodynamic transformations. Work and heat
Calorimetry - Isothermal processes. Phase changes - Heat transfer: Conduction, convection, radiation - Thermal expansion of solids and liquids

Ideal and Real Gases - Laws of gases. Equation of state of ideal gases - Constant volume ideal gas thermometer - Gas transformations. Work - Heat. Specific heats - Internal energy of the ideal gas - Study of some transformations - Cyclic transformations - Real gases. Equation of state. Internal energy - Van der Waals equation - pV diagrams. pT diagrams. Clapeyron's formula

Second Principle of Thermodynamics - Statements of the second principle of thermodynamics - Reversibility and irreversibility - Carnot's theorem - Absolute thermodynamic temperature - Clausius' theorem - The entropy state function - The principle of entropy increase - Calculation of entropy variations - Entropy of the ideal gas - Unusable energy
PVT Systems - Thermodynamic Potentials - Thermodynamic potentials - General properties of pVT systems - Maxwell relations

Electrostatic Force. Electrostatic Field - Electric charges. Insulators and conductors - Electrical structure of matter - Coulomb's law - Electrostatic field - Electrostatic field produced by a continuous charge distribution - Field lines of the electrostatic field - Motion of a charge in an electrostatic field.

Electrical Work. Electrostatic Potential - Work of the electric force - Voltage, potential - Calculation of electrostatic potential - Electrostatic potential energy - The field as a gradient of the potential - Equipotential surfaces - The curl of the electrostatic field - The electric dipole - The force on an electric dipole.
Gauss's Law - Flux of the electrostatic field - Gauss's law - Demonstration of Gauss's law - Some applications and consequences of Gauss's law - The divergence of the electrostatic field.
Conductors. Dielectrics. Electrostatic Energy - Conductors in equilibrium - Hollow conductor - Electrostatic shield - Capacitors - Connection of capacitors - Energy of the electrostatic field

Electric Current - Electrical conduction - Electric current - Stationary electric current - Ohm's law of electrical conduction - Resistors in series and parallel - Electromotive force - Generalized Ohm's law - Charging and discharging a capacitor through a resistor - Displacement current - Kirchhoff's laws for electrical networks

Magnetic Field. Magnetic Force - Magnetic interaction. Magnetic field - Electricity and magnetism - Magnetic force on a moving charge (Lorentz force) - Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor - Mechanical moments on planar circuits.

Sources of the Magnetic Field. Ampere's Law - Magnetic field produced by a current - Calculations of magnetic fields produced by particular circuits: straight wire (Biot-Savart Law), circular loop, infinite solenoid - Electrodynamic actions between current-carrying wires - Ampere's law - Gauss's law for the magnetic field.

Time-Varying Electric and Magnetic Fields - Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction - Origin of the induced electric field and the induced electromotive force - Applications of Faraday's law - Self-induction - Magnetic energy - Ampere-Maxwell's law - Maxwell's equations - Maxwell's equations in differential form.
assessment_rules: The exams consist of a written test and an oral test. The written test is divided into two parts; the first concerns mechanics, while the second concerns thermodynamics + electromagnetism. Both include the solution of problems on the topics covered during the exercises. It is possible to take the two different parts in different exam calls, as long as they are in the same session. The written part is passed if the average of all answers is above a minimum value, typically 15, but this value may vary depending on the difficulty of the questions. The oral test consists of a discussion of approximately 40-60 minutes covering four to six questions.
